mainEntity.name: Why do I get two different fiber numbers?

acceptedAnswer.text: The calorie-based figure (14 g per 1,000 calories) scales with your actual intake, while the IOM reference is a population guideline by age and sex that doesn't account for individual calorie needs — they're usually similar but can differ for atypical calorie intakes.

mainEntity.name: What happens if I increase fiber too quickly?

acceptedAnswer.text: A sudden large increase can cause digestive discomfort like bloating or gas. Increasing gradually over a few weeks, along with adequate water, generally helps your digestive system adjust.

mainEntity.name: Can I get too much fiber?

acceptedAnswer.text: The IOM did not set an upper limit for fiber from food. Very high intakes can cause discomfort, and people with some digestive conditions may be advised to limit fiber, so follow any guidance from your doctor or dietitian.
